Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
(a) In a directed weighted graph on |V| vertices, the cost of the operation for a vertex v is the number of outgoing edges from v (its out-degree). The worst possible single operation occurs when a vertex has outgoing edges to every other vertex in the graph, which is at most **|V| − 1**. Therefore, the cost of the worst possible single operation is |V| − 1.

(b) Using aggregate analysis, the total cost over the entire sequence of |V| operations equals the sum of the out-degrees of all vertices, which is equal to the total number of edges |E| in the graph. The average (amortized) cost per operation is:

|E| / |V|

Since |E| is at most |V|² (the maximum number of edges in a directed graph on |V| vertices), the average amortized cost is at most:

* (a) The worst possible single operation has cost |V| − 1 (a vertex connected to all other vertices).
* (b) The average amortized cost via aggregate analysis is |E|/|V| ≤ |V| − 1, since the total edges |E| ≤ |V|(|V| − 1) and we divide by |V|.

So the average amortized cost is **O(|V|)**, specifically bounded by |V| − 1.
